description: Menu bar icon highlight when gesture is engaged
steps: Modify Sources/Ledge/GestureController.swift - Add a callback property: var onEngagementChanged: ((Bool) -> Void)? and call it from apply(_:) when engagedControl transitions between nil and non-nil (on .engaged set to true, on .disengaged set to false).

Modify Sources/Ledge/MenuBarController.swift - Subscribe to controller.onEngagementChanged in init. When engaged (true): set statusItem.button?.contentTintColor to .controlAccentColor (or a suitable highlight color). When disengaged (false): set contentTintColor back to nil (restoring template appearance). This is called from the main thread (the event tap callback runs on the main run loop) so UI update is safe.
acceptance_criteria: The callback fires true on .engaged and false on .disengaged
MenuBarController subscribes and changes contentTintColor accordingly
Running `swift test` still passes all 54 tests
verification: Run `swift test` and confirm all 54 tests pass
findings: All 54 tests pass. Implementation straightforward - added onEngagementChanged callback to GestureController and subscribed in MenuBarController init to toggle contentTintColor.
